subject.title: [Bug]: project-local .env is ignored in 2026.3.28, OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH falls back to ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json

question: Should OpenClaw allow `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` from untrusted workspace `.env` files, and if so under what constraints?
rationale: Current source, tests, and public docs intentionally reserve the `OPENCLAW_` namespace for trusted process/global config, while the issue reports a real regression from the older project-local workflow.

options.title: Keep workspace `OPENCLAW_` blocked
options.body: Preserve the current fail-closed security boundary and point affected users at process env, global runtime dotenv, config `env`, or shell import instead.

options.title: Allow only config path
options.body: Permit a narrow `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` exception while keeping `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and other runtime-control keys blocked, with regression tests and docs updated together.

options.title: Add explicit opt-in trust
options.body: Introduce a maintainer-approved trusted-project mode before any workspace `.env` can steer OpenClaw runtime config paths.

recommendation.title: Keep workspace `OPENCLAW_` blocked
recommendation.body: Preserve the current fail-closed security boundary and point affected users at process env, global runtime dotenv, config `env`, or shell import instead.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored and merged the startup dotenv hardening that created the current trust boundary and are the strongest history signal for this decision.
